questions.question: The work done by a force is defined as the product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force. What is the unit of work?
questions.explanation:
Work is defined as force × displacement in the direction of the force. Its SI unit is the joule (J), where 1 J = 1 N·m (one newton-metre).

Why the others are wrong:
• Newton (N) is the unit of force.
• Watt (W) is the unit of power.
• Pascal (Pa) is the unit of pressure.

questions.question: A force of 10N moves a body through a distance of 5m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.
questions.explanation:
Using W = F × d × cos θ, with θ = 0° (force in the direction of motion), so cos 0° = 1.

W = 10 N × 5 m × 1 = 50 J.

questions.question: A body of mass 2kg is lifted through a height of 5m. Calculate the potential energy gained. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
Gravitational potential energy is P.E. = mgh.

m = 2 kg, g = 10 m/s², h = 5 m
P.E. = 2 × 10 × 5 = 100 J.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body of mass 4kg moving with a velocity of 3ms⁻¹ is
questions.explanation:
Kinetic energy K.E. = ½mv².

m = 4 kg, v = 3 m/s
K.E. = ½ × 4 × 3² = ½ × 4 × 9 = 18 J.

questions.question: Power is defined as the rate of doing work. Its S.I. unit is
questions.explanation:
Power = work ÷ time. Its SI unit is the watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.

Why the others are wrong:
• Joule = unit of energy/work.
• Newton = unit of force.
• Pascal = unit of pressure.

questions.question: A machine does 500J of work in 10s. Calculate its power.
questions.explanation:
Power P = W ÷ t.

P = 500 J ÷ 10 s = 50 W.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation:
Work is a scalar quantity — it has magnitude but no direction. It is the dot product of two vectors (force and displacement), which produces a scalar.

Why the others are wrong:
• Force, velocity, and acceleration are all vectors (they have both magnitude and direction).

questions.question: The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position is called
questions.explanation:
Potential energy is the energy a body possesses due to its position or state. For example, a raised object has gravitational potential energy (mgh), and a stretched spring has elastic potential energy.

Kinetic energy is due to motion. Thermal and chemical energies are internal forms of energy.

questions.question: A body of mass 5kg is moving with a velocity of 4ms⁻¹. Calculate its kinetic energy.
questions.explanation:
K.E. = ½mv².

m = 5 kg, v = 4 m/s
K.E. = ½ × 5 × 4² = ½ × 5 × 16 = 40 J.

questions.question: The work done in lifting a body of mass 10kg through a height of 2m is [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
Work done against gravity equals the gain in potential energy: W = mgh.

m = 10 kg, g = 10 m/s², h = 2 m
W = 10 × 10 × 2 = 200 J.

questions.question: A force of 20N acts on a body and moves it through a distance of 3m at an angle of 60° to the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.
questions.explanation:
W = F × d × cos θ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.

W = 20 N × 3 m × cos 60° = 60 × 0.5 = 30 J.

questions.question: The principle of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed but can be
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant — energy can only be transformed from one form to another (e.g., potential → kinetic → heat).

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.5kg is dropped from a height of 10m. Calculate its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
By conservation of energy, all the initial potential energy is converted to kinetic energy just before impact.

P.E. = mgh = 0.5 × 10 × 10 = 50 J = K.E. just before hitting the ground.

questions.question: The efficiency of a machine is 80%. If the work input is 500J, calculate the work output.
questions.explanation:
Efficiency = (work output ÷ work input) × 100%

80 = (work output ÷ 500) × 100
work output = (80 × 500) ÷ 100 = 400 J.

questions.question: A pump raises 200kg of water through a height of 10m in 20s. Calculate the power developed. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
Work done = mgh = 200 × 10 × 10 = 20,000 J.
Power = work ÷ time = 20,000 ÷ 20 = 1000 W.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a unit of energy?
questions.explanation:
The watt (W) is the SI unit of power, not energy. Power is the rate of energy transfer (1 W = 1 J/s).

The joule (J), kilowatt-hour (kWh), and electronvolt (eV) are all units of energy.

questions.question: A body of mass 2kg moves with a velocity of 5ms⁻¹. What is its momentum?
questions.explanation:
Momentum p = mv.

m = 2 kg, v = 5 m/s
p = 2 × 5 = 10 kg·m/s.

questions.question: The work done by a force of 100N in moving a body through a distance of 2m is
questions.explanation:
W = F × d (since force and displacement are in the same direction).

W = 100 N × 2 m = 200 J.

questions.question: A machine has a velocity ratio of 5 and an efficiency of 60%. Calculate its mechanical advantage.
A body of mass 10kg is raised to a height of 5m. Calculate the work done against gravity. [g = 9.8ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
W = mgh (work done against gravity).

m = 10 kg, g = 9.8 m/s², h = 5 m
W = 10 × 9.8 × 5 = 490 J.

questions.question: The energy stored in a stretched spring is
questions.explanation: A stretched or compressed spring stores elastic potential energy. This energy is released when the spring returns to its natural length. The formula is P.E. = ½kx², where k is the spring constant and x is the extension.

questions.question: A car of mass 1000kg accelerates from rest to 20ms⁻¹ in 10s. Calculate the average power developed.
questions.explanation:
Work done = change in K.E. = ½mv² − 0 = ½ × 1000 × 20² = 200,000 J.
Average power = work ÷ time = 200,000 ÷ 10 = 20,000 W = 20 kW.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation:
Force is a vector — it has both magnitude and direction.

Work, energy, and power are all scalars. Work and energy have magnitude only; power is a rate (scalar).

questions.question: A 50W electric bulb is used for 10 hours. Calculate the energy consumed in kWh.
questions.explanation:
Energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h)

Power = 50 W = 0.05 kW
Time = 10 h
Energy = 0.05 × 10 = 0.5 kWh.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body is 100J and its mass is 2kg. Calculate its velocity.
questions.explanation:
K.E. = ½mv²

100 = ½ × 2 × v²
100 = v²
v = 10 m/s.

questions.question: A force of 5N moves a body through a distance of 10m. If the work done is 25J, calculate the angle between the force and the displacement.
questions.explanation:
W = F × d × cos θ

25 = 5 × 10 × cos θ
25 = 50 cos θ
cos θ = 0.5
θ = 60°.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the work done by a force?
options: It is always maximum when the angle is 90°
questions.explanation: Work can be negative when the force opposes the displacement (θ > 90°). For example, friction does negative work. Also, W = Fd cos θ, so if θ = 180°, W = −Fd (negative).

questions.question: A body of mass 4kg falls freely from a height of 20m. Calculate its velocity just before hitting the ground. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
By conservation of energy: mgh = ½mv²

gh = ½v²
10 × 20 = ½v²
200 = ½v²
v² = 400
v = 20 m/s.

Alternatively, use v² = u² + 2gh with u = 0.

questions.question: The power of a machine is 2kW. How much work can it do in 30 minutes?
questions.explanation:
Power = 2 kW = 2000 W; time = 30 min = 1800 s.

Work = power × time = 2000 × 1800 = 3,600,000 J = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

questions.question: A machine with an efficiency of 75% is used to lift a load of 300N through a height of 5m. Calculate the work input.
questions.explanation:
Useful work output = load × height = 300 × 5 = 1500 J.

Efficiency = (work output ÷ work input) × 100%
75 = (1500 ÷ work input) × 100
work input = (1500 × 100) ÷ 75 = 2000 J.

questions.question: The energy possessed by a moving body is called
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses by virtue of its motion. It is given by K.E. = ½mv².

questions.question: A block of mass 2kg slides down a frictionless incline from a height of 1m. Calculate its speed at the bottom. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
By conservation of energy: mgh = ½mv²

gh = ½v²
10 × 1 = ½v²
v² = 20
v = √20 m/s.

questions.question: A force of 200N is applied to move a body through a distance of 5m. If the work done is 500J, calculate the angle between the force and the displacement.
questions.explanation:
W = F × d × cos θ

500 = 200 × 5 × cos θ
500 = 1000 cos θ
cos θ = 0.5
θ = 60°.

questions.question: The work done in stretching a spring by 0.1m is 2J. Calculate the spring constant.
questions.explanation:
Work done in stretching a spring = ½kx²

2 = ½ × k × (0.1)²
2 = ½ × k × 0.01
2 = 0.005k
k = 400 N/m.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation:
Coal is a fossil fuel and is non-renewable — it takes millions of years to form and cannot be replenished on a human timescale.

Solar, wind, and hydro are renewable — they are naturally replenished.

questions.question: A body of mass 5kg is moving with a velocity of 2ms⁻¹. Calculate its kinetic energy.
The efficiency of a machine is defined as
questions.explanation:
Efficiency = (useful work output ÷ total work input) × 100%.

Since work output is always less than work input (due to friction), efficiency is always less than 100%. Also equivalent to M.A./V.R. × 100%.

questions.question: A pump lifts 1000kg of water through a height of 20m in 50s. Calculate the power of the pump. [g = 10ms⁻²]
A body of mass 2kg is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 10ms⁻¹. Calculate the maximum height reached. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
At maximum height, all K.E. is converted to P.E.: ½mv² = mgh

½ × 2 × 10² = 2 × 10 × h
100 = 20h
h = 5 m.

Alternatively, using v² = u² − 2gh at v = 0: h = u²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct expression for power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, so Power = Work ÷ Time. Its SI unit is the watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.question: A machine has a mechanical advantage of 4 and a velocity ratio of 5. Calculate its efficiency.
questions.explanation:
Efficiency = (M.A. ÷ V.R.) × 100%

Efficiency = (4 ÷ 5) × 100% = 80%.

questions.question: The energy transformation in a hydroelectric power station is
questions.explanation:
In a hydroelectric station, water stored at a height has gravitational potential energy, which converts to kinetic energy as it falls, which then drives turbines to produce electrical energy.

So: Potential → Kinetic → Electrical.

questions.question: A body of mass 1kg falls from a height of 5m. Calculate its kinetic energy when it has fallen 2m. [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation:
The loss in potential energy equals the gain in kinetic energy.

Fall height = 2 m
K.E. gained = mgh = 1 × 10 × 2 = 20 J.

questions.question: The work done by a force of 10N in moving a body through a distance of 2m at an angle of 180° to the direction of the force is
questions.explanation:
W = F × d × cos θ, with θ = 180°.

cos 180° = −1
W = 10 × 2 × (−1) = −20 J.

Negative work means the force is opposing the motion.

questions.question: A 100W electric bulb is used for 5 hours. Calculate the energy consumed in joules.
questions.explanation:
Energy = power × time

Power = 100 W; time = 5 h = 5 × 3600 s = 18,000 s
Energy = 100 × 18,000 = 1,800,000 J = 1.8 × 10⁶ J.

questions.question: A body of mass 3kg is moving with a velocity of 4ms⁻¹. Calculate its momentum.
questions.explanation:
Momentum p = mv

p = 3 × 4 = 12 kg·m/s.

questions.question: The work-energy theorem states that the work done on a body is equal to the
questions.explanation: The work–energy theorem states: the net work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy, i.e. Wnet = ΔK.E. = ½mv² − ½mu².

questions.question: A machine is 60% efficient. If it is used to raise a load of 120N through a height of 2m, calculate the work input.
questions.explanation:
Useful work output = load × height = 120 × 2 = 240 J.

Efficiency = (work output ÷ work input) × 100%
60 = (240 ÷ work input) × 100
work input = (240 × 100) ÷ 60 = 400 J.

questions.question: A body of mass 2kg is lifted through a height of 10m. Calculate the potential energy gained. [g = 9.8ms⁻²]
Which of the following is an example of a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation:
Solar energy is renewable — it is continuously supplied by the sun and will not run out on a human timescale.

Natural gas, coal, and petroleum are fossil fuels and are non-renewable.
